components.name: top_level_matrix_compute_unit
components.description: Integrates instruction execution, configuration, scheduling, matrix storage, computation, DMA, status, and interrupt logic.

components.name: instruction_input_queue
components.description: Captures and holds 64-bit instructions presented with start, providing a stable instruction to the decoder and preventing loss during execution.

components.name: instruction_decoder
components.description: Decodes the 64-bit instruction into opcode, destination and source register identifiers, operation class, matrix dimensions, collective-operation attributes, and validity/error indications. Generates exactly one one-hot operation strobe for each supported opcode.

traceability.section: Functional Specification for Multi Core Matrix Compute Unit.

components.name: instruction_control_processor
components.description: Sequences instruction acceptance, operand preparation, execution launch, memory operations, barriers, and completion. Maintains the architectural busy, done, and error state.

components.name: architectural_register_file
components.description: Stores matrix register descriptors and metadata for registers M0 through M15, including base address, rows, columns, element type, and validity. Supplies derived dimensions to the decoder/control processor.

components.name: matrix_data_store
components.description: Provides on-chip buffering for active tiles, source operands, accumulators, and result tiles. Organizes storage by core and tile to support parallel access.

components.name: global_scheduler
components.description: Partitions matrix operations into tiles, distributes work across processing cores, coordinates collective operations, and tracks outstanding work.

components.name: work_stealing_scheduler
components.description: Maintains per-core work queues and permits idle cores to acquire pending tiles from other queues to improve load balance.

components.name: local_tiling_engine
components.description: Generates tile coordinates and local loop indices for matrices up to 32 by 32 and converts architectural matrix descriptors into core-local tile operations.

components.name: matrix_processing_cores
components.description: Replicates the matrix processing datapath across a configurable number of cores. Each core performs tiled matrix arithmetic and local data movement.

components.name: matrix_alu
components.description: Implements elementwise add, subtract, divide, multiply-accumulate, transpose, inverse support operations, determinant/reduction support, slice, concatenate, and identity/zero generation using 64-bit numerical operands.

components.name: fpu_64bit
components.description: Performs IEEE-compatible or implementation-defined 64-bit floating-point arithmetic for matrix addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, reduction, inverse, eigenvalue, and SVD support.

components.name: dma_engine
components.description: Moves matrix tiles between external memory and the on-chip matrix data store using the 512-bit AXI4 master read and write channels. Supports burst transfers, outstanding transaction tracking, and response/error capture.

components.name: interrupt_controller
components.description: Aggregates completion, fault, illegal instruction, DMA error, arithmetic exception, and barrier timeout events and presents a sticky interrupt status and interrupt output.

components.name: configuration_status_register_block
components.description: Implements the control/status register interface, captures software configuration, exposes execution status and counters, and provides software reset/interrupt controls.

components.name: error_and_assertion_monitor
components.description: Detects illegal opcodes, invalid dimensions, matrix-shape mismatches, AXI response errors, arithmetic exceptions, queue overflow/underflow, and collective-operation deadlock conditions.

protocol_rules.name: write transaction that is progressing to its final destination/write transaction that is progressing to its final destination p.93
protocol_rules.description:
If read data is obtained from a write transaction:
It must be obtained from the most recent version of the write.
The data must not be cached to service a later read.
Transactions are Modifiable, see A5.2.2 Modifiable transactions.
Write transactions can be merged.
For a Normal Non-cacheable Bufferable read, data can be obtained from a write transaction that is still progressing to its final destination. This data is indistinguishable from the read and write transactions propagating to arrive at the final destination at the same time. Read data that is returned in this manner does not indicate that the write transaction is visible at the final destination.
Write-Through No-Allocate
The required behavior for the Write-Through No-Allocate memory type is:
The write response can be obtained from an intermediate point.
Write transactions must be made visible at the final destination in a timely manner, as defined in the glossary. There is no mechanism to determine when a write transaction is visible at the final destination.
Read data can be obtained from an intermediate cached copy.
Transactions are Modifiable, see A5.2.2 Modifiable transactions.
Read data can be prefetched.
Write transactions can be merged.

protocol_rules.name: destination is permitted to wait for VALID to be asserted before asserting the corresponding READY/destination is permitted to wait for VALID to be asserted before asserting the corresponding READY p.54
protocol_rules.description:
If READY is asserted, it is permitted to deassert READY before VALID is asserted.
In Figure A3.4, both the source and destination happen to indicate that they can transfer the address, data, or control information after edge 1. In this case, the transfer occurs at the rising clock edge when the assertion of both VALID and READY can be recognized. These assertions mean that the transfer occurs at edge 2.
A3.2. Channel handshake

protocol_rules.name: caching Manager that receives snoop transactions/Store p.318
protocol_rules.description:
The action of a Manager component changing the value held at a particular address location. For a processor, a store occurs as the result of executing a particular instruction. Whether the store results in the Manager issuing a read or write transaction depends on whether the accessed cache line is held in the local cache, and if it is in the local cache, the state it is in.

An agent that receives and responds to requests.
